description: AI summaries lose the author's voice and quietly drop detail. Reframe takes the opposite promise: it never rewrites your material, it re-architects it into callouts, definitions, comparisons and steps.

The source is parsed and split into deterministically addressed units before any model runs. The model — Groq's llama-3.3-70b behind a rotating key pool — only returns block types and unit ids; the server rehydrates every word from the original.
Without an API key it runs in a clearly flagged demo mode on deterministic heuristics, so it always works and costs nothing to try. Analytics and feedback flow to a Google Sheet through Apps Script.

features.title: Lossless by construction
features.desc: The model has no channel to emit body text — it returns addresses — so paraphrase is structurally impossible rather than merely checked.

features.title: Coverage guarantee
features.desc: Every source unit must be referenced exactly once. Missing or duplicated content throws and the section falls back to plain text.

features.title: Quoted fragments
features.desc: Any number or date the model highlights must be a literal substring of its unit, or the block is demoted to prose.

features.title: Demo mode
features.desc: Works with no key and no cost, clearly labelled in the interface.

challenge: People read long material — papers, docs, articles — and AI summaries are the usual shortcut. But a summary paraphrases, drops detail, and can confidently state things the author never wrote.
Reframe set out to make long text easier to read without changing a single word of it: find the structure that was always implicit and make it visible.
architectureCaption: The browser holds the library; /api/transform parses, addresses and verifies; the model only ever sees numbered units and returns ids.

steps.title: Parse
steps.desc: Markup is structure, not content — headings, lists and tables are parsed directly rather than classified by a model.

steps.title: Address
steps.desc: Text is split into deterministically addressed units like p0 and l1_0.

steps.title: Classify
steps.desc: The model receives numbered units and returns block types, unit ids and short scaffolding words — about 15 output tokens per block.

steps.title: Verify
steps.desc: assertCoverage checks every unit is used exactly once; any highlighted value must be a quoted fragment of its unit.

steps.title: Rehydrate
steps.desc: The server rebuilds every body field from the source text, and the reader renders the blocks.

sceneCaptions: Source text re-architected into a callout, a definition and a comparison.
What the model actually returns: block types and unit ids, never text.
Under the hood: parse, address, classify, verify.

screens.caption: Reframe's paste-in screen (running locally in demo mode).

decisions.title: Addresses, not text
decisions.desc: Once the model can only return ids, verbatim stops being something to check and becomes a property of the architecture — and output cost drops sharply.

decisions.title: A verifier that can't fail isn't one
decisions.desc: An early fidelity check reported 100% verbatim while the model rewrote sentences in an unchecked field. Every guarantee now has a test that fails before its fix.

decisions.title: Plain-but-complete beats polished-but-lossy
decisions.desc: Any coverage or fragment violation demotes the block to prose instead of dropping or inventing content.

decisions.title: Write the divergence down
decisions.desc: An ADR described a pipeline that no longer existed. Recording what actually runs — and when it changed — is now part of the process.

roadmap: PDF and link ingestion polish for the students-first wedge.
Cross-device sync once the validation metric gates pass (v0 is localStorage-only).
Replace Sheets analytics with a real store after the gates pass.
